page: Amazon Web Services g6e.12xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and tailored for graphics-intensive and machine learning workloads. The host configuration features an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores running at 3.4 GHz, paired with 384 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz. Acceleration is delivered by four NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPUs providing a cumulative 179 GB of VRAM. The system is also equipped with 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a 100 Gbps baseline network throughput.

Benchmark data confirms exceptional performance in machine learning evaluation tasks. In large language model inference, the g6e.12xlarge achieves top-tier results (top 10%) across multiple model scales, reaching 13,220 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 135M model, 5,894 tokens per second on a 7B model, and 908 tokens per second on a 70B model. Text generation benchmarks show similar strength across model tiers. General compute metrics are consistently strong, with stress-ng single-core (2992.35) and multi-core (71794.0) placing in the top 25%, alongside Geekbench ray tracing (52896.0) and PassMark encryption tests (56880.16).

Hardware tradeoffs include an x86_64 architecture lacking AVX-512 and AMX extensions, relying instead on standard AVX instruction sets and GPU offloading for tensor computation. Given its high resource density across four discrete GPUs, high memory capacity, bundled high-capacity NVMe drive, and 100 Gbps networking, the instance delivers solid resource efficiency for multi-GPU inference pipelines, high-throughput model serving, 3D rendering, video processing, and distributed deep learning evaluation.
